annotations.title: Pick between two or three products

description: For two or three products, which one the written buy-or-wait rules put ahead, or that neither is ahead, optionally for a shopper who owns a device or uses iPhone or Android, with a budget. Each product comes with its verdict (buy_now, wait, skip, check_fit or not_enough_data), its fit with the phone given, today's retailer price and the reasons, each with its source and how sure iDevice is. A product that does not work with the phone given goes last; then the verdict decides, then the fit answer. Price alone does not put one ahead. When the rules leave two products level, review_tiebreak says whether outlets' published review scores separate them (at least two independent outlets that reviewed each, all one way, a clear margin) and lists the themes reviewers agree on, each with the outlets that reported it. purchase_today and product_for_you split the answer in two: the better purchase today on the rules, and the better product, named only on the phone or fit answer or on outlets' review scores, else No clear winner; where the companies' own figures lean one way, product_for_you says which product leads on which criteria, conditionally, and names no winner (lead null). A lead on the verdict alone (lead_basis timing) is about when to buy, not which product is better; a product that only reads BUY NOW or FINE TO BUY against NO RUSH is not a lead, and a product whose answer is not_enough_data (NEWER MODEL OUT, NOT ENOUGH DATA) is not out-bought unless the other product is its own newer model already out. The same comparison as the decision card on idevice.com. No model is involved. A line slug (for example 'samsung-galaxy-ring') names the line's newest model; when that model is not on sale the answer is for the newest model of the line that is, and resolved_to says which and why. With buyer_context, the answer also carries buyer_decision: the personal answer the idevice.com decision page for the same question gives for that context (a recommendation class, its rule_id, the decisive factors, the trade-offs, what would change it and what is unknown, each with its evidence), and buyer_decision_info with the same answer in plain words and the page it belongs to. buyer_decision.base_answers are that page's own answers, which can differ from this tool's answer for a phone platform or a budget given as arguments.

budget_usd.description: A price ceiling in US dollars

buyer_context.description: Optional. The shopper's own situation, in the closed grammar of the form on the idevice.com decision pages: { context_version: "buyer-context-v1", context, provenance }. context: currency "USD", risk_tolerance "normal", urgency (today, within_30_days, within_90_days or can_wait), priorities (up to three { id, importance }, importance must_have, high or medium; an id is a use or buying criterion the page can weigh, such as sleep, fitness or battery_life), hard_constraints (up to three: { id: "phone_platform", value: "iphone" or "android" }, { id: "no_subscription", value: true }, { id: "max_budget", value: a dollar amount }), cost_inputs (up to three { kind: offered_price, trade_in or required_accessories, amount, currency "USD", explicit_zero }), and optionally platform, expected_ownership_months (12, 24, 36 or 48), owned_condition and ecosystem_switch_willingness. Amounts are numbers from 0 to 100000 with at most two decimals. provenance: for each hard constraint, "hard_constraints:<id>": "selected" when the shopper stated it; a hard constraint without "selected" is not applied. The products come from this call's own arguments. A context outside the grammar is answered with buyer_decision_info naming the fields to fix, and the rest of the answer is unchanged. The context is used for this one answer and then dropped: it goes into no log.

owned_device_slug.description: A product_slug of a device the shopper already owns, e.g. 'iphone-17'

owned_platform.description: The phone platform the shopper uses
